newsitem.title: CANADA: Toronto stocks hit fifth record close of 1997.
newsitem.headline: Toronto stocks hit fifth record close of 1997.

text.p: Toronto's key stock index hit its fifth record close of 1997 on Monday, boosted by heavyweight gold stocks and the flow of money into tax-sheltered pension plans.
The Toronto Stock Exchange's 300 Composite Index rose 31.35 points to finish at 6140.93, surpassing the previous record close set on January 17.
The TSE 300 also set an intra-day high of 6144.85.
Nearly 99 million shares changed hands worth C$1.6 billion ($1.2 billion). Advancing stocks outnumbered declines 533 to 450 with 271 issues unchanged.
Market players are also watching the direction of U.S. interest rates with a two-day meeting of the U.S. Federal Open Market Committee set to start on Tuesday.
"People are expecting no change from the Fed," said Josef Schachter, president of Schachter Asset Management.
Schachter said money is flowing into mutual funds as Canadians scramble to contribute to tax-sheltered pension plans ahead of the March 1 deadline.
Toronto's 14 sub-groups were equally divided. Gold shares led the strong side, followed by utilities, transportation and banking. Weak sectors included oils, media and base metals.

* BCE Inc., Canada's largest publicly-traded firm, rose 1.70 to 69.55 on 1.9 million shares. The telecommunications firm was propelled higher by market expectations of continued strong earnings, traders said.
* Scott Paper Ltd. fell 2.90 to 23.10 after president David Erskine said the sale of the consumer products firm may not bring the C$26 ($19) a share price it reached last week.
* Precision Drilling Corp. jumped 4.10 to close at 65 on 82,000 shares after the company said it expected to rework its takeover bid for Kenting Energy Services Inc.
* Pure Gold Resources Inc. topped the most-active list, edging up 0.015 to close at 0.365 on 2.5 million shares.
